 Live radar: what arrived today (RADAR-001)

A second surface watches public regulatory and research sources and answers one question a day:
 what arrived that is worth a look? 

 Admission, not a river. Every record is judged on separate dimensions (source, domain,
 relevance, confidence, date precision). On a measured day 1,660 records arrived and 17 were
 worth reading; the feed says so instead of showing 1,660 rows.
 A daily digest on the front page: what arrived, the top five with one line each, safety
 and recalls, what waits for a human, and the caveats (future-dated records, near-duplicates,
 sources blocked by policy). Nothing in it is model-generated; every line points at a record
 you can open and check.
 Watchlists save the filter you are looking at, with a live count.
 Company pages answer "what happened at Philips recently", not "how many rows exist".
 A review workflow (NEW / REVIEWING / CONFIRMED / DISMISSED + note, with an audit trail).
 Human decisions live in their own human.db ; the evidence ledger stays append-only and is
 opened read-only by every web request, so no button can corrupt it.
 Export whatever you are filtered to as CSV or JSON, including your review decisions.
 Delivery by webhook or SMTP ( radar digest --webhook/--smtp- ), dry run by default.
 An MCP server ( python -m medradar.mcp server ) exposing five read-only tools so an agent
 can ask the same questions. Nothing in it can write.

See docs/features/001/CAPABILITIES.md for the API,
MCP.md for client configuration, and
DELIVERY.md for the scheduler example.
The capability scan behind these choices is in
docs/research/001/TOOL CAPABILITY SCAN.md.

 Product workbench (PRODUCT-001)

The repository now also ships a working analyst workbench , not only the research programme:
search a medical-technology company, read its FDA regulatory record, open the official evidence,
compare two companies on one explicit counting rule, and export a sourced report.

 

 Data : 91,457 FDA device records (510(k), PMA originals and supplements, recalls) for
 59 tracked organizations, collected from openFDA on 2026-11-14/15 and committed as a
 hash-addressed snapshot (snapshot 2026-11-14T22:09:22Z-openfda ).
 Evidence : every record keeps its official FDA identifier and URL; the evidence drawer shows
 the four separate time fields and the verbatim applicant string used for attribution.
 Honesty : unattributed applicant strings, explicitly rejected look-alike names, provisional
 attributions (1,410 of 1,590 spellings), source coverage differences and out-of-scope sources are
 all visible in the product, not hidden.
 Stack : FastAPI serving a React 19 + TypeScript + Vite build; one Python process, no database
 server and no paid infrastructure.

 Intelligence brief workbench (PRODUCT-004)

The product now answers a research question, not only a query. Brief ( /brief ) turns a company,
a comparison set or a PMA/K number into a sourced brief over 3, 5 or 10 complete calendar years:

 Definition first — the question, window, event types, counting rule, snapshot and ownership
 basis are stated on the brief and encoded in the URL.
 Evidence-backed findings — a small deterministic rule set (pathway concentration, year shift,
 PMA-family scale, recall dominance, specialty coverage, provisional attribution). Every finding
 lists its rule, inputs, cited official records, a "what this does not mean" clause and a link that
 reproduces the records.
 Technology areas that work — official FDA product-code families with the official classification
 name, alongside the specialty table. The FDA itself states "Unknown" as the specialty for many
 class III codes (2,520 of Medtronic's 3,426 window records), so the specialty table alone is not a
 technology view.
 Explain this difference — every comparison measure opens its definition, numerator,
 denominator, filters and the records behind it.
 Deliverables — company/comparison/device Markdown briefs, an Evidence Appendix CSV with one row
 per supporting record and its official URL, and a print stylesheet for browser PDF.
 Honest change status — a deployment without the DATA-001 ledger says so; it never presents an
 old record as "new".

Acceptance for this release (real Chromium, real snapshot, screenshots and downloads) is in
docs/product/product 004/ACCEPTANCE.md; the audit that
motivated it is in PRODUCT AUDIT.md.

 Workbench quick start

 

The committed snapshot and the committed web/dist let the product run offline, without Node and
without re-collecting. To refresh the data or rebuild the UI, see
docs/product/ARCHITECTURE.md 8.

 The product is deliberately snapshot-based : it never claims live or real-time data, and it
 makes no predictive claim. The research programme below is unchanged and still runs.

---

 Can public evidence see medical-technology change coming?

MedRadar collects free regulatory, clinical-trial and corporate-filing evidence about medical-device
and drug makers into one auditable event store, then tests — with frozen experiments, named baselines
and published negative results — whether that evidence carries signal before the market notices.

 Research infrastructure, not a validated predictive product. No method in this repository has
 demonstrated out-of-sample predictive ability, and the shipped snapshot cannot support genuine
 point-in-time claims. The engineering and the negative results are the deliverable.
 → Limitations · Method contract

 
 375,378 events · 6 free public sources · event dates 1966–2026 · snapshot 2026-10-31 · 1,160 offline tests · package v0.5.0 · MIT

install.title: Get started
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/ChazY11/medradar.git && cd medradar
pip install -e .                      # standard library only; no API key

python -m pytest -q -o addopts=""     # 1,160 offline tests at the verified baseline, no network
medradar demo                         # offline, committed snapshot, < 60 s → out/demo/index.html

A live radar run needs network (still no API key), about three minutes:

medradar run --months 24 --with-trade --with-dashboard
# → out/index.html · out/report_zh.md · docs/dashboard.html · docs/report.html · out/summary.csv

The 1.3 GiB SQLite snapshot is intentionally not committed, so a clean clone reproduces the procedure, not the exact numbers. The frozen studies rebuild from the recorded commands:

python -m medradar.intelligence.pipeline collect --source fda --months 120   # needs `.[bulk]`
python experiments/reverse_rd_v2/run_v2.py --db data/medradar.sqlite --holdouts 3
